definition: Tricking people into giving away information or access instead of hacking a system.
exampleSentence: Social engineering works because people want to be helpful and trust easily.

definition: An attack where someone secretly sits between two parties and reads or changes messages.
exampleSentence: On public Wi-Fi, a man-in-the-middle attack can expose your passwords.

definition: An attack that inserts malicious database commands into an input field.
exampleSentence: A simple SQL injection let the attacker download the whole customer table.

definition: Trying every possible password or key until the right one works.
exampleSentence: A brute force attack against short passwords can succeed in just a few minutes.

definition: A phishing attack written for one specific person or company.
exampleSentence: The spear phishing email used the name of my real manager and a real project.

definition: A phishing attack aimed at senior executives such as the CEO.
exampleSentence: Whaling attacks often ask a finance director to make an urgent bank transfer.

definition: Phishing carried out over a phone call or voice message.
exampleSentence: The vishing caller pretended to be from the bank and asked for a code.

definition: Phishing carried out through text messages.
exampleSentence: I received a smishing message that said my parcel was waiting behind a strange link.

definition: Inventing a believable story to make a victim share information.
exampleSentence: Through pretexting, the attacker called the help desk and pretended to be a new employee.

definition: Leaving something attractive, like an infected USB stick, to tempt a victim.
exampleSentence: The baiting attack started when someone found a USB drive near the elevator.

definition: Following an authorized person through a secured door without permission.
exampleSentence: Tailgating is easy when employees hold the door for people they do not know.

definition: Watching someone's screen or keyboard to steal passwords or private data.
exampleSentence: Use a privacy screen to protect yourself from shoulder surfing in busy cafes.

definition: Searching through trash to find documents with useful information.
exampleSentence: Dumpster diving is the reason why we shred every paper with names on it.

definition: A scam where an attacker uses a hacked or fake business email to steal money.
exampleSentence: A business email compromise attack cost the company two hundred thousand dollars last year.

definition: Registering a domain with a common spelling mistake to trick visitors.
exampleSentence: Typosquatting domains look almost the same as the real website at first glance.

definition: An attack that infects a website often visited by the target group.
exampleSentence: In the watering hole attack, the hackers infected a news site that engineers read daily.

definition: Trying stolen username and password pairs on many different websites.
exampleSentence: Credential stuffing succeeds when people reuse the same password everywhere.

definition: Trying a few common passwords against many accounts to avoid lockouts.
exampleSentence: Password spraying is hard to notice because each account gets only one attempt.

definition: A program or device that secretly records every key a user presses.
exampleSentence: The antivirus found a keylogger that had been recording her passwords for weeks.

definition: Software that secretly collects information about a user's activity.
exampleSentence: The free app hid spyware that sent browsing history to an unknown server.

definition: Software that shows unwanted ads and often tracks user behavior.
exampleSentence: The browser became slow after the adware installed itself with a free tool.

definition: Malware that hides itself deep in the system and keeps privileged access.
exampleSentence: A rootkit can hide its files even from the operating system tools.

definition: Malware that pretends to be a useful program to trick the user into installing it.
exampleSentence: He downloaded a cracked game, but it was a trojan that opened his computer to attackers.

definition: Malware that copies itself and spreads across networks without user action.
exampleSentence: The worm spread to hundreds of computers within minutes of the first infection.

definition: A network of infected devices controlled by an attacker.
exampleSentence: Thousands of hacked cameras were part of the botnet that attacked the website.

definition: A hidden way to enter a system while avoiding normal security checks.
exampleSentence: The attackers left a backdoor so that they could return after we fixed the bug.

definition: A small malware program whose only job is to install other malware.
exampleSentence: The email attachment was just a dropper that fetched the real ransomware later.

definition: Harmful code that runs only when a certain condition or date is reached.
exampleSentence: The angry developer planted a logic bomb that deleted files after his last day.

definition: Secretly using someone's computer to mine cryptocurrency.
exampleSentence: The sudden CPU spikes on our servers were caused by cryptojacking.

definition: Malware that runs in memory and leaves almost no files on the disk.
exampleSentence: Fileless malware is difficult to find because traditional scanners look for files.

definition: Malware designed to destroy data permanently instead of asking for a ransom.
exampleSentence: The wiper erased the boot sector and left hundreds of machines unusable.

definition: Fake warnings that scare users into buying useless or harmful software.
exampleSentence: A pop-up claimed the laptop had fifty viruses, but it was only scareware.

definition: Malware that gives an attacker full remote control of the victim's computer.
exampleSentence: A remote access trojan let the attacker watch the employee's screen all day.

definition: Malware built to steal passwords, cookies and saved data from a device.
exampleSentence: The infostealer copied browser cookies and sent them to a criminal forum.

definition: Spreading malware through online advertisements.
exampleSentence: Malvertising can infect a computer even when the user visits a trusted website.

definition: An automatic malware download that happens just by visiting a webpage.
exampleSentence: A drive-by download installed the malware as soon as the page finished loading.

definition: Malware that changes its own code to avoid detection by antivirus tools.
exampleSentence: Polymorphic malware creates a new version of itself every time it spreads.

definition: Techniques malware uses to detect and avoid analysis in a test environment.
exampleSentence: The sample used sandbox evasion and stayed quiet until it was on a real laptop.

definition: The servers an attacker uses to send orders to infected devices.
exampleSentence: The firewall blocked traffic to a known command and control address.

definition: The stage of an attack when the harmful code is delivered to the victim.
exampleSentence: Payload delivery usually happens through an email attachment or a hidden download link.
